meta.name: Mamíferos
meta.description: La diversidad, adaptabilidad, comportamiento social y distribución geográfica de los mamíferos.

videos.title: A Winning Design
videos.overview: From the tiniest bat to the massive blue whale, all mammals share the ability to nurture their young on milk and regulate their own temperatures.

videos.title: Insect Hunters
videos.overview: Mammals from tiny shrews to giant anteaters have specialised in eating insects. Some have even pursued their prey into the skies.

videos.title: Plant Predators
videos.overview: The plant eaters take on the largely indigestible, spiny and poisonous defences of plants with some spectacular physical adaptations to diet.

videos.title: Chisellers
videos.overview: Special tools like chisel sharp front teeth and underground dwelling enable this group of mammals to feast on roots and seeds.

videos.title: Meat Eaters
videos.overview: Predators and prey must evolve speed, endurance and manoeuvrability to outwit each other, and the pack hunters must maintain order in the ranks.

videos.title: Opportunists
videos.overview: A mammal capable of having a varied diet can be highly adaptable and exploit new environments including the cities where they thrive.

videos.title: Return to the Water
videos.overview: With perfect streamlined bodies and great underwater speed, seals, dolphins, porpoises and whales became the new hunters of the sea..

videos.title: Life in the Trees
videos.overview: A range of adaptations from sucker-feet to gripping tails help the tree dwellers to survive, and in the dark forest super senses come in to play.

videos.title: Social Climbers
videos.overview: In the daily hubbub of monkey life, only those with a talent for social wheeler dealing get ahead, driving the shift towards larger brains.

videos.title: Food for Thought
videos.overview: The natural world was transformed when one great ape began to walk upright - us. But why has this led to the development of our extraordinary brains?
